copayment.reason: Primary policy wording plus corroborating CIS do not provide sufficient operative product-level copayment evidence.

protocol_outcome.reason: The preregistered protocol requires an inconclusive result when authoritative evidence is insufficient to score one or more target concepts and no architecture failure has otherwise occurred. Tata waiting_period demonstrated frozen-runtime CONFIG_SPEC reuse, while copayment remained a governed KNOWLEDGE_GAP.

observations: The experiment demonstrated generic-runtime reuse for a broad waiting-period concept without runtime modification.
The fail-closed knowledge boundary worked: missing copayment evidence did not become 0%, DOES_NOT_APPLY, or an authoritative absence claim.
The preregistered REUSE versus CONFIG_SPEC wording overlaps around product-specific spec instances; the conservative CONFIG_SPEC score was retained and the protocol was not edited mid-experiment.
A future repeatability experiment should clarify that classification boundary before product selection.
